q: A problem B is NP-complete when…
options: B is in NP and every problem in NP reduces to B in polynomial time
B reduces to every problem in NP
explain: NP-complete = in NP + NP-hard. Nobody has proved that NP-complete problems need exponential time.

q: What does the Cook–Levin theorem state?
options: Every NP problem can be solved in exponential time
explain: It was the first NP-completeness proof. Every later one reduces from SAT, directly or through a chain of reductions.

q: To show that a new problem B is NP-hard, you reduce…
options: a known NP-complete problem to B
B to a known NP-complete problem
B to a problem in P
explain: A ≤ₚ B means B is at least as hard as A. Reducing B to SAT would only show B ∈ NP.

q: If A ≤ₚ B and B can be solved in polynomial time, what follows?
options: A can be solved in polynomial time
explain: Transform the A instance in polynomial time, then run B's algorithm.

q: In the 3-SAT to CDP reduction, two literal-vertices are joined by an edge when…
options: they are in different clauses and are not x and ¬x
they are in the same clause
explain: A clique then picks one non-contradictory literal from each clause.

q: A formula has k clauses. The CDP instance asks for a clique of what size?
explain: One vertex per clause: one true literal in each clause.

q: G has n vertices and a clique of size k. What does its complement G′ have?
options: A node cover of size n − k
A node cover of size k
A clique of size n − k
explain: The vertices outside the clique touch every edge of G′, because G′ has no edge inside the clique.
False. 2-SAT is solvable in linear time with an implication graph and strongly connected components. 3-SAT is NP-complete.

q: Every NP-hard problem is in NP.
explain: False. The halting problem is NP-hard but undecidable. Optimisation versions of NP-complete problems are NP-hard but are not decision problems.

q: If someone found a polynomial-time algorithm for the node cover decision problem, what would follow?
options: Only NCDP would be in P
explain: NCDP is NP-complete, so every problem in NP reduces to it.
